**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/26 (Fri) 04:24
- [PREFERENCE] User is thinking of improving the lighting in their dining room.
- [PREFERENCE] User is considering adding under-cabinet lighting to supplement the chandelier.
- [PREFERENCE] User is unsure if under-cabinet lighting will be worth the investment.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Under-cabinet lighting enhances ambiance and functionality in a dining room.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Under-cabinet lighting refers to lighting installed under cabinets or shelves, providing task or ambient lighting.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Types of under-cabinet lighting include:
  - Linear LED strips
  - Puck lights
  - Strip lights
  - Tape lights
  - Recessed lights
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Benefits of under-cabinet lighting include:
  - Ambiance creation
  - Task lighting
  - Accent lighting
  - Increased safety
  - Flexibility
  - Energy efficiency
  - Hiding clutter
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Considerations for under-cabinet lighting include:
  - Cost
  - Installation
  - Design
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Simple installations (linear LED strips or tape lights) can cost between $120-$250.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Mid-range installations (puck lights or strip lights) can cost between $250-$500.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Complex installations (recessed lights or custom designs) can cost $500-$1,000 or more.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Factors affecting installation cost include complexity, location, existing electrical infrastructure, number of lights, and type of cabinets.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips to save money on installation include choosing simpler installations, DIY installation, shopping around, and considering a hybrid approach.
- [USER] User expresses concern about installation cost and complexity.
- [USER] User requests rough estimates for the cost to install under-cabinet lighting in an average-sized dining room.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] For puck lights, installation involves mounting with clips or adhesive, wiring to a low-voltage power source, and spacing them 12-18 inches apart.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Puck lights are small, round, and compact, providing focused task lighting.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Puck lights can be adjustable, dimmable, and available in various styles, including fixed and wireless options.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Color temperatures for puck lights include:
  - Warm White (2700K-3000K)
  - Soft White (3000K-3500K)
  - Bright White
